title: How do I accept x402 payments in XRP on my own API?
abstract: Sourced guide for an API owner: the 402 challenge to send, how a signed XRP Payment is verified and settled on XRPL Testnet, and which checks stop a retry from charging twice.
body:
Your API answers an unpaid request with HTTP 402 and a PAYMENT-REQUIRED header that quotes an exact XRP amount in drops, your account as payTo and network xrpl:1 for Testnet. The client retries with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE carrying a signed Payment, and your facilitator checks the terms, submits it and serves the resource only after a validated tesSUCCESS. [1] [2] [3] According to the XRPL x402 scheme, native XRP amounts are quoted in integer drops. [2]

The Starter Kit's payment integration, the x402-xrpl package, implements the exact scheme for native XRP Payments, and the t54 reference documents that scheme and its verify and settle steps. ResearchAgent's writers run this flow: each writer hosts its own facilitator, quotes 1,000 drops per Singapore cent and binds article, version and passage commitment into the invoice. [2] [3] [4]

Check every retry before you serve: the payee, exact amount, network, invoice and expiry must match your quote, and a resubmitted signed transaction must return the same response instead of a second charge. Settlement is final only in a validated ledger. The tested compatibility covers native XRP exact payments; it does not establish RLUSD or escrow support with external facilitators. [3] [4] [5]

Author interpretation: start on Testnet with faucet XRP, keep each quote and signed transaction so a timeout never becomes a second payment, and add key-reveal escrow only if your buyers need payment bound to delivery. Testnet XRP has no real value. Sources accessed 11 November 2026. [3] [4]
